Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 22:14:00 -0700
Subject: Nightly backfill — intermittent late closures, asking for SLA tolerance/keys

Hi Karthik,

We're seeing our nightly backfill (job type: user-profile-merge) cross the configured closure window about 2–3x/week over the last month. These are not tokenization errors — the executor is getting preempted mid-run on spot capacity, and the retry system ends up doing duplicate writes if the client retries without a deterministic idempotency key.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a temporary tolerance/credit for job finalization time while we work on migrating to persistent instances? We need a contractual acknowledgement that a small percentage of nightly runs may finish outside the 02:00–04:00 completion envelope during this migration period.
2) We also need clear guidance from your infra team on idempotency key shape and TTL for safe client retries (we'd like to implement this in our orchestrator this week).

I attached the current job spec for context (nightly_job_spec_v2.pdf). Can we get a short proposal this week? We're on a renewal cadence and want to avoid an escalation.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
SRE Lead, DataCompany

- What constitutes a single logical run (how clients mark job-run ids),
- Recommended idempotency key format and TTL for safe-at-least-once retries.

Best,

Hi Marta, Karthik — dug into the job spec and recent logs (INF-5123) this morning. TL;DR: we can support a safe contract and practical guidance without code changes on the Redwood side; a small client-side change plus a bounded SLA amendment will reduce risk.

Technical recommendations (for your orchestrator):
- Idempotency key: 128-bit hex (RFC 4122 v4 style UUID is fine) with the format: jobName:runId:attemptChecksum (example: profile-merge:20270518-02:1f4e2c8a).
- Server-side dedupe TTL: store keys for 7 days; this covers late replays and human-driven retries during migration.
- Retry policy recommendations: exponential backoff starting at 30s, max backoff 20m, cap retries at 6 attempts.
- Finalization semantics: we can mark a run as "committed" once KV write ACKs are persisted; clients should treat an ACK as definitive and avoid blind retries. If a client cannot obtain an ACK due to preemption, the client must include the idempotency key on retry so dedupe logic prevents double-commit.

SLA amendment suggestion (editable):
- Scope: job class = nightly backfill (as defined in nightly_job_spec_v2.pdf).
- Migration window: 2027-05-15 -> 2027-06-14 (30 days).
- Completion envelope: standard = 02:00–04:00 PST. Temporary tolerance = 04:00–06:00 PST. Runs finishing in tolerance window will be eligible for a one-time service credit equal to 50% of per-run compute charge, subject to a monthly cap of 25 runs per calendar month.
- Exclusions: incidents caused by customer-side misconfiguration or client not attaching idempotency keys will not be eligible.

Attachments: redwood_sla_draft_DC-3742.docx (I put the suggested amendment language in section 2).

Notes/risks: If we extend dedupe TTL beyond 7 days the backend storage growth and cost increase must be discussed — 7 days is a reasonable compromise. If you want longer retention we can do it but will need a pricing conversation.

Happy to join your sync to walk through the flow and confirm wording.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
